proposed_comments.title: Keep IconBox XamlRoot subscriptions and stale unload handling consistent
proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:**
- `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Controls/IconBox.cs` — `OnLoaded`, `OnUnloaded`, and the tracked `XamlRoot` lifecycle

**Problem:** The current head subscribes to the visible XamlRoot directly on every load and does not consistently clear or rebind the tracked root when the control unloads or rebinds. The stale-unload guard also depends on the active-demand state, so a rebound control can incorrectly treat a valid unload as stale.

**Why it matters:** Repeated load cycles can duplicate Changed callbacks, unsubscribe the wrong root after a root transition, or invalidate a rebound control after its request has already completed.

**Suggested change:**
1. Track the current XamlRoot explicitly, unsubscribe the previous root before subscribing to a new one, and clear the tracked root on unload.
2. Treat any loaded, in-bounds unload as stale even when _activeRequestDemand is already null and keep the lifecycle guard idempotent across rebinds.
3. Add or extend the lifecycle regression coverage to confirm repeated load/unload transitions do not duplicate callbacks or stomp the current root.

**Verification:** Run the exact-head CmdPal icon tests and the lifecycle regression coverage; verify repeated load/unload transitions do not duplicate XamlRoot callbacks or invalidate a rebound control.

The exact-head logic remains vulnerable to duplicate callbacks and rebound invalidation during repeated load cycles.

proposed_comments.title: Use the current diagnostics session accessor and release the demand reserve during completion
proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:**
- `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Helpers/Icons/IconLoadDiagnostics.cs` — `BeginSpeculativeDispatchDeferral`, `GetCurrentSession`, and `IsCurrentSession`
- `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Helpers/Icons/IconLoadQueue.cs` — `Complete()` and `_workerSlotsReservedForDemand`

**Problem:** Speculative deferrals still read _activeSession directly in the ETW-only path, bypassing the GetCurrentSession()/IsCurrentSession(...) identity checks. Completion also leaves _workerSlotsReservedForDemand active even after it drains accepted speculative work, so shutdown can stall while the reserve still blocks dispatch.

**Why it matters:** ETW-only listeners lose their speculative-deferral measurements, and accepted speculative work can remain stranded behind a stale demand reserve during shutdown.

**Suggested change:**
1. Use the current-session accessor for ETW-only speculative deferrals and keep the validity check aligned with the same session identity rules as the rest of the diagnostics lifecycle.
2. Release the demand reserve during completion and stop recording reserve deferrals once accepted speculative work has drained, then add a shutdown regression test proving the queue can finish.
3. Validate the queue with the exact-head completion regression covering the two-worker speculative drain case.

**Verification:** Run the CmdPal icon and queue tests and verify the ETW-only speculative measurement path and the completion-with-speculative-work regression both pass without shutdown stalls.
